summary: Research report for the orchestrate-centric core consolidation design. Answers all 7 research questions with file+line evidence: /orchestrate is missing --team, --hard/--fast, model flags, --clean, --force, --roadmap, and any phase-forcing or revision-with-reason mechanism at the command layer; skill-orchestrate dispatches agents directly (bypassing skill-researcher/planner/implementer), which silently drops memory retrieval and --lit resolution from every /orchestrate-driven task; /orchestrate --hard has no dispatch site anywhere (skill-orchestrate-hard is currently unreachable); hard-mode skill/agent pairs are structurally near-identical to base (cheap to collapse); only 3/19 extension manifests declare routing_hard; team mode has one historical use (task 36) and zero for team-plan/team-implement; next_artifact_number auto-increments for research only, not plan/implement; a 32-task Phase B evidence table is included with informal category assignment, file_scope, and BLOCKING-candidate flags for #68 and #81 (beyond the two the task description already named).

artifacts.summary: Phase A/B research input report: entry-point collapse gap analysis, phase-forcing flag mechanics, hard-mode duplication measurement, team-mode fold evidence, extension blast radius count, preserved-assets file+line table (including two confirmed-absent mechanisms: --lit resolution and memory retrieval on the /orchestrate path), and a 32-task Phase B evidence table.

memory_candidates.content: skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md dispatches research/plan/implement agents directly via the Agent tool (subagent_type: $RESEARCH_AGENT etc.), never through skill-researcher/skill-planner/skill-implementer. Those three skills are the sole location of Stage 4a (memory-retrieve.sh + clean_flag gating) and the lit-stage4a-flow.md interactive --lit resolution. Consequence: /orchestrate-driven tasks get zero memory-augmented context, and --lit is threaded as a boolean end-to-end but never resolved into an actual briefing -- it silently no-ops. Any future orchestrate-engine consolidation must rebuild these two mechanisms into skill-orchestrate's own dispatch-prep stage, not assume they carry over from the wrapping skills.

/orchestrate --hard has no dispatch site anywhere in the codebase: skill-orchestrate-hard/SKILL.md exists, is exercised by 10+ test/lint scripts, and is referenced in docs (hard-mode-routing.md claims it is 'invoked by /orchestrate --hard'), but no command file or script ever invokes it. Grepping commands/ and scripts/ for the skill name turns up only cross-references. This is a currently-dead, fully-built code path -- confirm reachability with a direct invocation-site grep before assuming any --hard command-level flag exists for /orchestrate.

next_artifact_number (specs/state.json per-task counter) is incremented only by research's postflight (orchestrator-postflight.sh, 'research only' comment); plan and implement read it back via a 'prev' mode (next_artifact_number - 1) and never increment it themselves. Any design for forced/repeated plan or implement phases must add new increment logic -- the append-vs-overwrite MM_ numbering behavior is asymmetric today, not uniformly append-safe across phases.
